hypothesis: In every bare trace the model sweeps A then B row by row (8+8 queries) and reaches C with 2 queries, so 6 of C's 8 cells in the final guess are unobserved defaults. Showing per-circuit query counts plus the fact that the budget cannot cover 24 rows each turn, and listing all answers by circuit at the final turn, will make a prompt-responsive solver (the real 7B) query all three circuits before the budget runs out (falsifiable: on a real-solver run, the fraction of episodes with some circuit at <=2 queries drops vs bare). Also: no final guess contradicts an observed answer, and none is unparsable.
behavior_changes: Each per-turn prompt appends: 'Queries per circuit so far: A=.., B=.., C=..', a note that the remaining queries cannot read every row so the inventory must be used to infer rows, and which circuits have not been queried yet
The final-guess turn includes a ledger of every observed answer grouped by circuit (benchmark wording) before the benchmark's last-turn prompt
The final guess is parsed; if it is missing or contradicts any observed answer, the model is re-asked once with the specific contradictions listed
Cells the environment answered are written into the returned 24-bit guess from the answers; all unobserved cells are the model's
preserved_behaviors: Benchmark system prompt, first message, answer wording and 'N queries remaining' lines unchanged
The model writes every query; a turn with no parsable query is still spent (no second chance), as in bare
One query per model call, never more than env.budget queries; BudgetExhausted/any query error ends the loop as in bare

With the scripted 'sequential' mock, the final guesses match bare's exactly on all 5 instances (the mock ignores prompt text and does not misreport the bits it saw), so this batch shows only that the plumbing works, not any gain
Checked res_11 trace: turn prompts show counts like 'A=5, B=0, C=0 ... circuit(s) B, C not queried yet'; the final prompt lists A/B/C answers

Unit test with a fake env: a guess that contradicts the answers -> re-asked once and observed cells patched; unparsable -> re-asked once and the second guess used; both unparsable -> raw text returned without a crash
risks: The coverage note is only a prompt change: a 7B model may ignore it, and this mock batch cannot measure whether it helps
Mentioning the inventory could push the model toward wrong structural guesses for unqueried rows instead of querying them
The re-ask adds at most one extra model call per episode; patching observed cells makes a guess self-consistent but does not make unobserved cells correct
Longer per-turn prompts add context for a 7B model over 18 turns
